picks.editorial_note: An international team led by TU Wien physicist Mario Krenn showed in Nature that AI can design novel physics experiments that outperform human-designed setups, a striking demonstration of AI accelerating fundamental science rather than just analyzing its outputs.
picks.title: Artificial Intelligence Suggests New Physics Experiments

picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen's Nature-published 'HydroGym' platform trains reinforcement-learning agents to actively control fluid dynamics, opening a path to AI control systems for energy, transportation, and defense applications far beyond the lab.
picks.title: Training AI Agents that Can Actively Control Fluid Dynamics in Energy, Transportation, and Defense | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: EPFL's framework for training AI to express calibrated 'doubt' addresses a core reliability problem in AI-driven science, letting models flag uncertainty rather than confidently propose bad experiments.
picks.title: An AI capable of doubt can optimize scientific discovery

picks.editorial_note: HKUST's GSCo framework, pairing a generalist medical AI with lightweight specialists, tackles the accuracy-versus-efficiency tradeoff that has limited clinical deployment of large medical AI models.
picks.title: Novel AI Framework Unites Generalist and Specialist Models for Precision Healthcare
picks.university: Hong Kong Univ. of Science and Technology

picks.editorial_note: A new $30 million NSF Science and Technology Center spanning eight institutions signals sustained federal investment in AI-driven turbulence modeling, with implications for energy efficiency and flight design.
picks.title: New Center Seeks to Unlock the Science of Turbulence for Energy, Flight, and Discovery

picks.editorial_note: UT Austin's fusion seed grants ride a wave of investment tied to DOE's Genesis Mission, which is explicitly funding AI to accelerate fusion research — a notable case of federal policy directing AI toward energy goals.
picks.title: Fusion Energy Seed Grants Launch New Interdisciplinary Collaborations at UT Austin - UT News
picks.university: The University of Texas at Austin

picks.editorial_note: A $2.88 million DOE award to a University of Houston-led team applies AI to reduce U.S. reliance on foreign-controlled rare-earth supply chains, tying AI research directly to critical national economic security priorities.
picks.title: Department of Energy Awards UH-led Team $2.88M to Use AI to Strengthen America’s Critical Mineral Supply Chain | University of Houston

picks.editorial_note: A four-year, $7.7 million partnership between Kansas engineers, the Army Corps of Engineers, and DHS to build AI-integrated digital twins of dams shows sustained cross-agency collaboration on critical infrastructure safety.
picks.title: Four years later KU researchers continue their work strengthening American dams

picks.editorial_note: Kent State's DOE Genesis Mission-funded project to mine 50 years of water-chemistry data into a continental-scale AI framework illustrates how federal AI initiatives are being extended to environmental monitoring.
picks.title: Streams Never Lie; Kent State Magazine; Fall 2026

picks.editorial_note: Federal cancellation of AHRQ healthcare research grants, including a Johns Hopkins AI project aimed at speeding cancer diagnosis, illustrates how shifting federal funding policy can abruptly halt promising applied-AI work.
picks.title: Funding cuts hit research focused on making American healthcare safer, more efficient
